CSCI 300 · Lab 3

Learn Linux Commands, Then Complete the Student Tasks

Continue from Week 2: edit a file, copy and rename it, read and search its content, delete temporary folders safely, and find help for Linux commands. Read each lesson, try the examples, then complete the clearly marked student tasks in your own Ubuntu Terminal.

5 illustrated lessons5 student tasks5 screenshot slotsInteractive command practiceDownloadable report

🎯 Learning outcomes

01 · Edit and organize

Edit and manage files with nano, cp and mv.

02 · Read and search

Read, search and count text using cat, head, tail, less, grep and wc -l.

03 · Delete and get help

Remove temporary files and folders safely, and find help with man and history.

Why are we learning this? Operating Systems is not only about theory. The Terminal lets us interact directly with files, folders, users and system information. Linux command-line skills are also useful in servers, cloud computing, virtual machines, containers, cybersecurity and software development.
